title: Etorobong Edet on LinkedIn
author: Etorobong Edet
author_headline: E-commerce Virtual Assistant | Product Listing | Order Processing | Store Management | Web Design | AI Workflow Automation
snippet:
Most websites are finished...

But the business behind them is still running manually.

The developer delivers the project.

The client celebrates the launch.

Then reality begins.

Every new lead gets copied into a CRM by hand.

WhatsApp messages are answered one by one.

Appointments are confirmed manually.

Invoices are chased.

Follow-up emails are forgotten.

The website is live.

The operations are not.

I think we've normalized delivering websites without delivering systems.

Imagine if every website launch also meant:

→ Leads automatically reaching the right salesperson.
→ Customers receiving instant WhatsApp updates.
→ Bookings creating calendar events automatically.
→ Payments triggering onboarding without human intervention.
→ AI handling routine customer enquiries 24/7.

That's the gap I'm focused on solving.

I'm currently looking to collaborate with web developers and digital agencies who want to offer clients more than a beautiful website.

You build the front end.

I'll build the operational engine that runs behind it.

Not as a competitor.

As your post-launch automation partner.

If you're a developer who believes a website should actually help run a business not just represent one, I'd love to connect.

title: Spanky The Sparky on LinkedIn
author: Spanky The Sparky
snippet:
People overcomplicate social media.

The next generation doesn’t care about polished. They care about authentic. They want to hear from real people with real experience, not another perfectly scripted corporate ad.

You don’t need a $10,000 camera. You don’t need a production studio. You don’t need an agency charging five figures to produce content that looks exactly like everyone else’s.

I’ve got an iPhone, a chair in my garage, and a pair of two-year-old safety glasses. That’s been enough to reach hundreds of millions of people.

What I find interesting is watching organizations spend thousands on marketing agencies that churn out generic content, then wonder why engagement is flat and recruiting isn’t improving.

Even more confusing is seeing organizations send people to membership development conferences year after year, while the very people responsible for membership development barely use social media themselves. Then they turn around and ask the members in the field to create the content that actually connects with people.

If your job is membership development, then developing membership should include meeting the next generation where they already are. In 2026, that’s not optional. It’s part of the job.

The trades don’t have a marketing problem. They have an authenticity problem.
